findings.checklist_item: Extend the Cluster-1 analysis and its pinning-test AC to cover binding_store (also string-gated at typed_dispatch.py:129), confirming that after **_kwargs normalization the set of kwargs each leaf receives is verified — not just repo_root.
evidence: typed_dispatch.py:129: `accepts_binding_store = "binding_store" in sig.parameters or _has_var_kw` — same string-introspection pattern the plan flags for repo_root
typed_dispatch.py:131-135 fallback comment: 'only leaves that explicitly declare it consume it — ticket 1577'
Plan lists only 'client' (unconditional) and 'repo_root' (string-gated) as the two hazards; binding_store is unmentioned
findings.finding: The Cluster-1 mechanism enumerates only two string-introspected kwargs (client, repo_root) but a third, binding_store, is gated by the identical runtime string check at typed_dispatch.py:129; a **_kwargs normalization flips accepts_binding_store to True for every leaf, so leaves that (per ticket 1577) were deliberately NOT passed binding_store will now receive it. It is benign because ignored, but the plan neither notes it nor pins it in the AC.
findings.location: CLUSTER-1 section; AC 'Cluster-1 is resolved...typed_dispatch.py:128's introspection still selects the right handlers'
scenarios: After **_kwargs normalization, every leaf's _has_var_kw is True, so binding_store is forwarded to all ten leaves including those that ticket 1577 intended to exclude
findings.suggested_fix: Add binding_store to the Cluster-1 hazard list alongside repo_root, and amend the AC to require the pinning test assert the forwarded-kwargs set (client, repo_root, binding_store) is unchanged in effect for all ten leaves.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add binding_store (typed_dispatch.py:129, :140-141) to Cluster-1's string-introspection hazard inventory and extend the AC#2 pinning test to assert that **_kwargs normalization does not change which leaves receive binding_store (not just repo_root).
evidence: Plan: 'repo_root is gated by runtime string introspection (typed_dispatch.py:128: accepts_repo_root = "repo_root" in sig.parameters or _has_var_kw). Renaming flips this to False'
Plan AC#2: 'if **_kwargs normalization is chosen, typed_dispatch.py:128's introspection still selects the right handlers and a test pins it' — names only :128 (repo_root), not :129 (binding_store)

typed_dispatch.py:129: accepts_binding_store = "binding_store" in sig.parameters or _has_var_kw; :140-141 conditionally add binding_store to _leaf_kwargs; :135 fallback sets accepts_binding_store = False
apply_inbound.py:66 declares binding_store and :88-124 consume it — a leaf that currently gets binding_store only because it declares the name
findings.finding: Cluster-1's introspection-gated-parameter inventory names only two of the three parameters that typed_dispatch.py selects by runtime string introspection. It cites client (typed_dispatch.py:137) and repo_root (typed_dispatch.py:128) as the hazards but omits binding_store, which is gated by the identical pattern at typed_dispatch.py:129 (accepts_binding_store = "binding_store" in sig.parameters or _has_var_kw) and passed at :140-141. Normalizing all ten leaves to **_kwargs flips _has_var_kw to True, which flips accepts_binding_store to True for every leaf and starts passing binding_store to leaves that never declared it (the signature-inspection fallback at :135 deliberately sets it False for exactly this reason).
findings.location: CLUSTER-1 — reconciler leaf handlers, 'Two hazards that make a naive rename unsafe' + AC#2
scenarios: Under **_kwargs normalization, _has_var_kw is True for every leaf, so accepts_binding_store (typed_dispatch.py:129) becomes True for the outbound leaves that never declared binding_store; the dispatcher now passes binding_store into them where it previously did not — a silent dispatch-behavior change the plan's hazard list and AC#2 test scope (repo_root only) do not cover, risking violation of AC#7 'No behaviour change'.
